land.text: Jutland and the Danish islands, the Danish part of the minor kingdoms before Gorm 'reigning from c. 936'

predecessors.note: The sister dossier records the 936 loss of the Danish core to Denmark; the pages opened here do not describe the petty kingdoms before Gorm.

land.text: Schleswig round Hedeby, which Cliopatria gives to Denmark in 936

predecessors.note: The kingdom-of-germany dossier has a 936 loss of Schleswig; none of the pages opened here dates the Mark of Schleswig, so this handover rests on Cliopatria's shapes.

land.text: Denmark inside the union of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, 'Incorporated into the Kalmar Union: 17 June 1397'

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps a 73 km2 Danish sliver to 1406 and draws the union from 1402; the kalmar-union dossier starts on 17 June 1397.

capitals.name: Jelling
capitals.note: The page: Gorm 'ruled from Jelling'; the infobox as returned reads 'Jelling (until 10th cent.)'. The end year is the researcher's bridge to Sweyn's accession c. 986.

capitals.name: Roskilde
capitals.note: Infobox as returned: 'Roskilde (since 10th cent.)'; Sweyn Forkbeard page: 'The main centres of Danish power shifted from Jutland to the towns of Roskilde and Lund' (undated). Valdemar IV 'made Vordingborg his personal residence' and was 'the first Danish king to rule from Copenhagen' (both undated); the start year 986 is a bridge.

rulers.name: Gorm the Old
rulers.note: 'reigning from c. 936 to his death c. 958'.

rulers.name: Sweyn Forkbeard
rulers.note: 'Around 986 Swein revolted against his father' and took the throne; died at Gainsborough on 3 February 1014.

rulers.name: Harald II
rulers.note: 'Harald II died in 1018, and Cnut went to Denmark to affirm his succession'.

rulers.name: Cnut the Great
rulers.title: king of Denmark, England and later Norway

rulers.name: Harthacnut
rulers.note: Succeeded in Denmark in 1035; 'until his death in 1042'.

rulers.name: Magnus the Good
rulers.note: The Magnus article was not opened: 1042 follows Harthacnut's death (Cnut page), 1047 is 'In 1047 Magnus died' (Sweyn II page).

rulers.name: Sweyn II Estridsson
rulers.note: 'King of Denmark from 1047 until his death in 1076'; the chronicles wrongly say 1074.

rulers.name: Canute VI
rulers.note: 'King of Denmark from 1182 to 1202'; died 12 November 1202.

rulers.name: Valdemar II
rulers.note: 'King of Denmark from 1202 until his death in 1241' (28 March 1241).

rulers.name: Christopher II
rulers.note: 'Christopher II (1319-1332)'; the interregnum that follows ('For eight years after Christopher's death, Denmark had no king') has no entry.

rulers.name: Valdemar IV
rulers.note: Acclaimed at Viborg on 24 June 1340; died at Gurre on 24 October 1375 (the footer says 25 October).

rulers.name: Margaret I
rulers.title: regent
rulers.note: 'after his early death in 1387 she took on the role herself (1387-1412)'; the entry stops where the Kalmar Union takes over.

keyframe_review.note: 57,037 km2: Denmark's 184 cells and 24 in Schleswig-Holstein (the Hedeby border country). The page: Gorm 'reigning from c. 936 to his death c. 958', 'He ruled from Jelling'; it also says 'Between c. 960 and the early 980s, Harald Bluetooth appears to have established a kingdom' and 'united ... in 965', so this is Gorm's realm. Infobox area (S1, Danish Realm): modern Denmark 42,926 km2, no medieval figure or year. Ratio 1.33 to the modern country, within a factor of two. The pages do not give the 936 frontier: extent unverified.

57,143 km2, the same lands. The Harald Bluetooth page puts his accession at c. 958 (infobox 'c. 958 - c. 986'); nothing on the pages changes the extent in 947. Infobox area (S1, Danish Realm): modern Denmark 42,926 km2, no medieval figure or year. Unverified beyond the reign dates.

82,635 km2: adds Scania (56 cells), Halland (26) and Blekinge (13). The Harald page cites the Curmsun disc calling him 'king of Danes, Scania, Jomsborg' (undated); the Sweyn Forkbeard page says 'Swein was able to extend Danish control east of the strait of Oresund into Skane' (also undated), so the year 960 is Cliopatria's and the two pages disagree on which king added Scania. Kept.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, valid 970-994: Denmark with Scania, Halland and Blekinge and Norway under Harald, then under Sweyn as overlord 'c. 986 - c. 994'

keyframe_review.note: 110,227 km2: adds 119 cells of Norway (77 of them Viken) and 28 more Swedish cells. Harald page: infobox Norway 'c. 970 - c. 985/986', the Jelling stone says he 'won the whole of Denmark and Norway', but the lead says his rule there was 'most likely lasting for no more than a few years in the 970s' and that after the 974 defeat 'he no longer had control of Norway'. The Sweyn Forkbeard page makes Sweyn 'overlord of Norway c. 986 - c. 994'. Kept as Cliopatria draws it but only to 994, not 989 (the 990 row drops Norway too early).

correction.text: the shape unchanged, valid 995-1002 (Norway outside the Danish shape; from 1000 it is a vassal, see the ledger)

keyframe_review.note: 82,592 km2: Denmark with Scania, Halland, Blekinge, no Norway. Valid for 995-1002 only: the Sweyn Forkbeard page makes him overlord of Norway to c. 994 and again 'from c. 1000' (Battle of Svold, 999 or 1000). The 1000-1014 overlordship is a vassal tint in the ledger, not part of the shape. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 995..1002 from this entry's own 'Valid for 995-1002 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]
82,855 km2, the same lands (one cell more). Sweyn Forkbeard's reign 986-1014; the page dates only his 1005 return from England. Kept.

146,440 km2: Denmark plus 264 cells of southern England (bbox west to -3.2E). The Cnut page: Cnut landed at Sandwich 'early in September 1015' and 'Wessex ... submitted to Cnut late in 1015', so the shape is right from late 1015; the north of the Thames follows in the autumn of 1016 (ledger gain), the whole kingdom on 30 November 1016, Cnut crowned in 1017. Harald II ruled in Denmark ('Harald II died in 1018'). The same English land is also in the kingdom-of-england row for these years.

correction.text: Denmark under Harthacnut after Cnut's death: Jutland, the islands, Scania, Halland, Blekinge and the Schleswig border land as in the 1056 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1035-1039, years Cliopatria leaves to its North Sea Empire row (to 1039) although the empire ended with Cnut's death on 12 November 1035: 'In Denmark, he was succeeded by Harthacnut'. Cliopatria has no Danish shape between 1018 and 1055, so Denmark alone in these years is drawn from the 1056 shape. Harthacnut joins the English crown in 1040 (ledger).

correction.text: Denmark under Sweyn II Estridsson from 1047, separate again from Norway

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1047-1055: Cliopatria draws this land inside its Norway-Denmark row to 1055, but the Sweyn II page has 'In 1047 Magnus died' and Sweyn 'King of Denmark from 1047'; Harald Hardrada, not Magnus, ruled Norway. The land is the 1056 shape.

82,592 km2: Denmark with Scania, Halland, Blekinge and the Schleswig border land. Sweyn II 'King of Denmark from 1047 until his death in 1076'; the page describes wars with Harald Hardrada (Hedeby sacked 1050, Nisa off Halland 1062, peace 1064) but no change of frontier; 'Eventually he managed to return and establish a foothold in Scania' is undated. Kept for 1056-1146.

82,635 km2, the same lands (two more Schleswig cells than in 1056). The History of Denmark page says nothing dated in 1147; the change is a Cliopatria boundary tweak on the Schleswig border that no page explains. Kept.

correction.text: the Danish core without Rugen (Rugen is the vassal principality-of-rugen from 1168)

keyframe_review.note: 87,209 km2: the core plus 13 cells of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, which is Rugen. The page: 'In 1168, Valdemar and Absalon gained a foothold on the southern shore of the Baltic' and 'the Rugian principality stayed with Denmark until 1325'. Rugen has its own dossier (principality-of-rugen, a Danish vassal from 1168), so it is removed here and carried as a vassal in the ledger.

correction.text: the Danish core without the Mecklenburg and Pomeranian lands (vassals from 1185 only)

keyframe_review.note: 111,138 km2: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern grows from 13 to 87 cells and 29 cells of Brandenburg come in. The Canute VI page dates only the Pomeranian overlordship to 1185 ('in 1185 forced Bogislaw to acknowledge Canute as his overlord'); the History of Denmark page says 'In the 1180s, Mecklenburg and the Duchy of Pomerania came under Danish control'. Those are vassals (mecklenburg, pomerania), so they are removed from the shape and carried by vassal events from 1185; Cliopatria's 1177 start is eight years early.

correction.text: the Danish core without the vassal lands of Mecklenburg, Pomerania and Rugen

keyframe_review.note: 137,988 km2: adds 101 cells of Poland (the Pomeranian duchy) on top of the 1177 lands. Pomerania was an overlordship from 1185, not Danish territory: 'Canute ordered two invasions of Pomerania and in 1185 forced Bogislaw to acknowledge Canute as his overlord'. Removed from the shape and carried as a vassal (duchy-of-pomerania, whose dossier starts in 1188).

correction.text: the Danish core with Holstein and Lubeck, without the vassal lands of Mecklenburg, Pomerania and Rugen

keyframe_review.note: 149,954 km2: adds Holstein and Lubeck (Schleswig-Holstein 68 cells, Hamburg 3). Valdemar II page: 'In 1203 Valdemar invaded and conquered' Lubeck and Holstein (its lead gives 1207; Stellau was in 1201); the Canute VI page has the count surrender his lands north of the Elbe in 1203. Cliopatria's 1202 is one year early. Holstein and Lubeck kept, the vassal lands removed.

correction.text: the Danish core with Holstein, Lubeck and the Saaremaa cells (unverified), without the vassal lands

keyframe_review.note: 153,844 km2: as 1202 plus 15 cells of Saaremaa (Saare). The Valdemar II page does not mention a 1206 expedition to Saaremaa (unverified: page budget); the Saaremaa cells are kept as Cliopatria draws them. The vassal lands are removed as in 1202.

correction.text: the Danish core with Holstein and Lubeck, without the vassal lands

keyframe_review.note: 150,168 km2: Saaremaa gone again. The page: 'In 1216, Valdemar II and his Danish troops ravaged the County of Stade and conquered Hamburg' (Cliopatria has three Hamburg cells from 1202, fourteen years early). The vassal lands are removed as in 1202.

correction.text: the Danish core with Holstein, Lubeck and Hamburg, without Estonia (danish-estonia) and the vassal lands of the Wendish coast

keyframe_review.note: 164,308 km2 (the maximum): adds 61 cells of northern Estonia. The page: 'the establishment of Danish rule in Estonia in 1219' (Lindanise, 15 June 1219). Estonia has its own colony dossier (danish-estonia), so it is carried as a vassal tint; the vassal lands of the Wendish coast are removed.

correction.text: the Danish core after Bornhoved: Denmark, Scania, Halland, Blekinge and the Schleswig border land, without Estonia and Rugen (vassals)

keyframe_review.note: 164,152 km2: still all the north German lands. The page: the Battle of Bornhoved on 22 July 1227 'cemented the loss of Denmark's north German territories'; Cliopatria keeps them to 1235. The shape from 1227 is the 1236 land without Estonia and Rugen (both carried as vassals). The page is silent on whether Estonia was lost in 1227 (the danish-estonia dossier has it so): not recorded here.

correction.text: the Danish core without Estonia and Rugen

keyframe_review.note: 101,408 km2: the German lands are gone (so the German side is right) but Estonia (60 cells) and Rugen (13 cells) are still inside. Estonia is the colony danish-estonia and Rugen the vassal principality-of-rugen, so both are removed. The Treaty of Stensby (1238) is not on the pages opened (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: the Danish core without Estonia and Rugen

keyframe_review.note: 101,144 km2, same lands as 1236. Nothing on the pages opened dates a change in 1250 (unverified: page budget). Estonia and Rugen removed as in 1236.

correction.text: the Danish core without Estonia and Rugen, to the loss of Scania in 1332

keyframe_review.note: 100,985 km2, same lands. The page: 'the Rugian principality stayed with Denmark until 1325'. Estonia and Rugen removed (vassals), valid to 1332.

correction.text: Denmark proper and the Schleswig border land without Scania, Halland, Blekinge and Gotland, which were not Danish until 1360-1361

keyframe_review.note: 87,067 km2: Denmark with Scania, Halland, Blekinge and 15 cells of Gotland. The page: under Christopher II 'most of the country was seized by the provincial counts (except Skane, which was taken over by Sweden)' and 'For eight years after Christopher's death, Denmark had no king'; the Valdemar IV page lists Halland, Blekinge and Scania among lands Valdemar later captured and has him 'invaded Gotland in 1361'. So all Swedish cells are removed for 1333-1343 (Swedish until 1360).

correction.text: Denmark proper without the southern-Jutland cells held by danish-magnates and without Estonia (danish-estonia)

keyframe_review.note: 66,497 km2: Denmark without 12 southern-Jutland cells (the Danish Magnates row) plus 60 cells of Estonia. Valdemar IV page: infobox 'Duke of Estonia 1340-1346', Zealand retaken in 1346, 'North Friesland was recovered in 1344'. Estonia is carried by the colony dossier, so it is removed; the Jutland cells stay with danish-magnates to 1351.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, valid 1352-1359 (Scania, Halland and Blekinge return in 1360, Gotland in 1361)

keyframe_review.note: 57,754 km2: Denmark proper (the Jutland sliver is back) without Scania or Gotland. Valid for 1352-1359: the page has Valdemar force 'Magnus to give up Helsingborg in 1360' and invade Gotland 'in 1361'; the two gains are ledger events and the 1363 shape draws their result. The History of Denmark page: the recovery of the territories 'was finally completed in 1360'.

87,067 km2: Denmark, Scania, Halland, Blekinge, Gotland and the Schleswig border land, the result of the 1360 and 1361 gains. The page also has the Hanseatic alliance of 1362, Valdemar's flight at Easter 1368 and the Treaty of Stralsund in 1370 but no territorial term (any Hanseatic hold on the Scanian castles is not on the page).

correction.text: Denmark, Scania, Halland, Blekinge, Gotland and the Schleswig border land, without Greenland

keyframe_review.note: 95,434 km2: the 1363 land plus 20 cells of Greenland. The Danish Realm page: 'The Faroe Islands and Greenland have been under the Crown of Denmark since 1397'; before that Greenland was a Norwegian crown land (see the norse-greenland dossier, which has its 1261 subordination to Norway). Greenland removed.

correction.text: as 1363, without Greenland or Norway, valid 1395-1396

keyframe_review.note: 95,830 km2: as 1385 plus a Norwegian cell. Valid for 1395-1396 only: the History of Denmark page has the Kalmar Union 'made official in 1397' ('Incorporated into the Kalmar Union: 17 June 1397'), and the kalmar-union dossier draws 1397-1401. Greenland and the Norwegian cell removed. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1395..1396 from this entry's own 'Valid for 1395-1396 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: nothing: the row draws no Danish land after 1397; the Kalmar Union draws it

keyframe_review.note: 73 km2 near 65.6N 26.0E in Finland, nowhere near Denmark: a stray sliver. Denmark has been part of the Kalmar Union since 17 June 1397 (page); the union's own dossier draws the land. The correction is empty on purpose and the validator's --resolve warning 'resolves to no cells' is expected.

region.text: Jutland and the Danish islands round Jelling, with the Schleswig border land (Hedeby)

ledger.note: 936: Gorm the Old reigns from Jelling and the Danish kingdom begins. The page: 'reigning from c. 936 to his death c. 958', 'He ruled from Jelling'. It also says the Danes 'were united and officially Christianized in 965 AD by Gorm's son Harald Bluetooth' and the Danish Realm infobox gives 'Unification: c. 965'; the year is the page's c. 936, the land is read from Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: Scania, Halland and Blekinge, 95 cells of Cliopatria's 960 shape

ledger.note: 960: Scania, Halland and Blekinge pass to the Danish crown in Cliopatria. The Harald Bluetooth page names Scania among the lands of the 'king of Danes' on the Curmsun disc (undated) and gives his reign as c. 958-986; the Sweyn Forkbeard page credits Sweyn with extending 'Danish control east of the strait of Oresund into Skane'. The year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Norway as Cliopatria draws it in 970-989 (119 cells, 77 of them Viken)

ledger.note: c. 970: Harald Bluetooth rules Norway as well as Denmark. Infobox 'Norway c. 970 - c. 985/986', the Jelling inscription says he 'won the whole of Denmark and Norway', with Haakon Sigurdsson as de facto ruler; the lead says the rule lasted 'no more than a few years in the 970s'. The year is c. 970; the Norwegian cells are Cliopatria's.

region.text: Haithabu and the Dannevirke, the Schleswig frontier

ledger.note: 974: Otto II takes Hedeby and the Danevirke. 'Otto II counter-attacked Harald in 974', 'conquering Haithabu, Dannevirke and possibly large parts of Jutland' (the page is cautious on Jutland). Cliopatria does not show the loss.

region.text: the part of the Hedeby-Dannevirke frontier regained in 983 ('some of the seized territory')

ledger.note: 983: Harald regains part of the lost frontier. 'Harald regained some of the seized territory in 983', after Otto II's defeat; the page does not say which part.

c. 986: the Danish seat moves from Jelling to Roskilde. The History of Denmark infobox gives 'Jelling (until 10th cent.)' and 'Roskilde (since 10th cent.)'; the Sweyn Forkbeard page: 'The main centres of Danish power shifted from Jutland to the towns of Roskilde and Lund' (undated). The year is the bridge to Sweyn's accession c. 986.

region.text: Norway as drawn in the 970-989 shape, outside the Danish shape from 995

ledger.note: 995: the Danish overlordship of Norway lapses. The Sweyn Forkbeard page: 'He was also overlord of Norway c. 986 - c. 994 and from c.1000'; the gap is the rise of Olaf Tryggvason (old-kingdom-of-norway has him proclaimed in 995, from a page not opened here).

region.text: Norway under Hakon's sons Erik and Swein as Sweyn's jarls

ledger.note: c. 1000: Sweyn is overlord of Norway again. 'In 999 or 1000, Swein defeated Olaf at the naval Battle of Svold', and after it 'he appointed Hakon's sons, Erik Hakonsson (his son-in-law) and Swein Hakonarson to rule as jarls'. The page does not split Norway among the victors.

region.text: England, from the landing at Sandwich

ledger.note: August 1013: Sweyn Forkbeard invades England. 'Swein returned to England in August 1013 with his younger son Cnut'; 'By December he had achieved full control and was acknowledged as king'. England is drawn contested, as the kingdom-of-england dossier does.

region.text: England, abandoned by the Danes in 1014

ledger.note: 3 February 1014: Sweyn dies at Gainsborough and the Danish hold on England ends. 'Swein's rule was very short-lived, as he died at Gainsborough on 3 February 1014'; 'the English magnates recalled Aethelred' and he 'drove Cnut out of England' (both undated). The year and the death are the page's, the end of the hold is read from them.

region.text: Norway, no longer under Danish jarls

ledger.note: 1015: Norway leaves the Danish overlordship. The Sweyn Forkbeard page is silent on Norway after 1013 ('does not discuss Norway after Swein's death'); the date is the old-kingdom-of-norway dossier's (Olaf Haraldsson from 1015), a page not opened here, and Cliopatria's Norwegian row.

region.text: England, from Cnut's landing at Sandwich

ledger.note: September 1015: Cnut lands at Sandwich. 'In the summer of 1015, Cnut's fleet set sail for England with a Danish army of perhaps 10,000 in 200 longships'; 'early in September 1015' he 'came into Sandwich, and straightway sailed around Kent to Wessex' (Peterborough Chronicle).

region.text: Wessex, which 'submitted to Cnut late in 1015'

ledger.note: Late 1015: Wessex submits to Cnut. 'Wessex ... submitted to Cnut late in 1015' (the page's wording). This is the English part of Cliopatria's 1015 shape (264 cells).

region.text: all of England north of the Thames

ledger.note: Autumn 1016: England north of the Thames goes to Cnut. After Assandun ('On 18 October 1016, the Danes were engaged by Edmund's army'), 'all of England north of the Thames was to be the domain of the Danish prince' and the south stayed with Edmund 'along with London' (the Deerhurst arrangement, undated; the year is implied by the page). Reviewer eu-14-d: region narrowed from all England to Mercia, Northumbria and East Anglia, the land north of the Thames the Cnut page gives.

region.text: England, now under Cnut alone

ledger.note: 30 November 1016: Edmund dies and Cnut is king of all England. 'Edmund died on 30 November, within weeks of the arrangement' (the year is implied; the Sweyn Forkbeard page has 'Cnut became king of all England'); the coronation followed 'in London in 1017'.

region.text: England south of the Thames and London

ledger.note: 30 November 1016: the rest of England, south of the Thames and London, comes to Cnut with Edmund's death.

region.text: Denmark and England, the lands Cnut held in 1017

ledger.note: 1018: Cnut takes the Danish crown and the realm becomes the North Sea Empire. 'Harald II died in 1018, and Cnut went to Denmark to affirm his succession to the Danish crown'; 'His later accession to the Danish throne in 1018 brought the crowns of England and Denmark together.' Denmark and England are drawn by north-sea-empire until Cnut's death.

region.text: Denmark under Harthacnut, as the 1056 shape

ledger.note: 12 November 1035: Cnut dies and Denmark has its own king again. 'Cnut died on 12 November 1035 in Shaftesbury, Dorset'; 'In Denmark, he was succeeded by Harthacnut, reigning as Cnut III.'

region.text: Denmark in Harthacnut's union with England, 1040-1042

ledger.note: 1040: Harthacnut joins England to Denmark. 'Harold Harefoot ... reigning until his death in 1040'; Harthacnut 'brought the crowns of Denmark and England together again until his death in 1042'. The dossier denmark-england draws the union (month 6, from a page not opened here).

region.text: Denmark under Sweyn II, as the 1056 shape

ledger.note: 1047: Magnus dies and Sweyn Estridsson is king of Denmark. 'In 1047 Magnus died, having stated on his deathbed that his kingdom would be divided'; Sweyn was 'King of Denmark from 1047 until his death in 1076'. Denmark is separate again; Norway goes to Harald Hardrada.

region.text: Rugen: the 13 cells of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern in the 1169 shape

ledger.note: 1168: Valdemar and Absalon subdue Rugen. 'In 1168, Valdemar and Absalon gained a foothold on the southern shore of the Baltic'; 'the Rugian principality stayed with Denmark until 1325'. The principality is a Danish vassal (principality-of-rugen, whose page has the feudal homage).

region.text: the duchy of Bogislaw I

ledger.note: 1185: Bogislaw I of Pomerania becomes Canute VI's vassal. 'Canute ordered two invasions of Pomerania and in 1185 forced Bogislaw to acknowledge Canute as his overlord'; Barbarossa had demanded in 1184 that Canute acknowledge him as liege. Counterpart: the duchy that Cliopatria's 'Pomerania' row (to 1187) becomes in 1188.

region.text: Mecklenburg, the Obotrite lands of the princes of Mecklenburg

ledger.note: 1180s: Mecklenburg comes under Danish control. The page: 'In the 1180s, Mecklenburg and the Duchy of Pomerania came under Danish control, too'; no year is given, 1185 is the bridge with the Pomeranian date.

region.text: Holstein, Lubeck and Hamburg, the north German frontier

ledger.note: 1201: Valdemar takes the field against the Holstein count. 'He defeated and captured the count at the Battle of Stellau in 1201.' The page does not say how the count of Holstein stood to the Empire; holy-roman-empire is the counterpart as in its own dossier.

region.text: Holstein, Lubeck and Hamburg, the north German frontier

ledger.note: 1203: the fighting over Holstein and Lubeck ends in a Danish conquest. 'In 1203 Valdemar invaded and conquered' Lubeck and Holstein (the page's lead gives 1207); the Canute VI page: 'the count had to turn over all his lands north of the Elbe to Duke Valdemar in 1203'.

region.text: Holstein north of the Elbe and the city of Lubeck

ledger.note: 1203: Holstein and Lubeck come under the Danish crown. 'In 1203 Valdemar invaded and conquered Lybeck and Holstein'; Cliopatria's shape begins in 1202.

region.text: Hamburg

ledger.note: 1216: Hamburg falls to Valdemar II. 'In 1216, Valdemar II and his Danish troops ravaged the County of Stade and conquered Hamburg'; two years later the emperor 'was rewarded with the emperor acknowledging Denmark rule of Schleswig and Holstein' (the page's wording, the year inferred from 'Two years later').

region.text: northern Estonia: Harria, Vironia and Jerwia, the 60 Estonian cells of Cliopatria's 1220 shape

ledger.note: 15 June 1219: Danish rule is established in northern Estonia. 'the establishment of Danish rule in Estonia in 1219'; 'on 15 June 1219 while the Danes were attending mass' the Estonians attacked and the Battle of Lindanise was won, and Valdemar ordered a fortress at Reval. The page names Estonia, not its provinces; the dominion is the colony danish-estonia. The page is silent on the loss to the Brothers of the Sword in 1227 and the Treaty of Stensby in 1238 (the danish-estonia dossier has both); not recorded here.

region.text: Holstein, Lubeck and Hamburg, the Danish holdings south of the Eider

ledger.note: 1223: the German war begins with the king's capture. 'In 1223, King Valdemar and his eldest son, prince Valdemar, were abducted by Count Henry I of Schwerin'; the page puts the Danish defeat at Molln in 1225 and the release is undated. The year is the page's, the fighting zone is the holy-roman-empire dossier's.

region.text: Holstein, Lubeck and Hamburg

ledger.note: 22 July 1227: the Battle of Bornhoved ends the Danish hold on north Germany. The page: 'culminating in the Battle of Bornhoved on 22 July 1227 cemented the loss of Denmark's north German territories'.

region.text: Holstein, Lubeck and Hamburg, the north German territories lost

ledger.note: 22 July 1227: Holstein, Lubeck and Hamburg are lost at Bornhoved. 'cemented the loss of Denmark's north German territories' (the page does not itemise them; Cliopatria keeps them to 1235).

region.text: Mecklenburg

ledger.note: 1227: Danish overlordship of the Wendish coast ends with Bornhoved. The page names no Wendish prince; 'the loss of Denmark's north German territories' includes the Mecklenburg overlordship, which the page does not mention.

region.text: the duchy of Pomerania

ledger.note: 1227: Danish overlordship of Pomerania ends with Bornhoved ('all of the Wendish lands and Pomerania' had been acknowledged as Danish about 1218, per the same page).

region.text: Rugen and its mainland

ledger.note: 1325: the Rugian principality leaves the Danish tie. 'the Rugian principality stayed with Denmark until 1325'.

region.text: Scania, Halland and Blekinge, 95 cells of the 1285 shape

ledger.note: 1332: Scania passes to Sweden. Under Christopher II (1319-1332) 'most of the country was seized by the provincial counts (except Skane, which was taken over by Sweden)'; the page does not date the transfer within the reign. Halland and Blekinge are listed among lands Valdemar IV later captured (Valdemar IV page, undated). The year is the end of the reign, the Sweden dossier's date for Scania and Blekinge.

region.text: the Danish core Valdemar IV rebuilt from the mortgaged parcels

ledger.note: 24 June 1340: Valdemar IV is acclaimed king and the kingdom re-forms. 'at the Viborg Assembly (landsting) on St John's Day (St Hans' Day) on 24 June 1340'; Denmark 'had been without a king for years' and 'was mortgaged out in parcels'. The recovery of the pledged lands took until 1360 (History of Denmark: 'finally completed in 1360'). Reviewer eu-14-d: counterpart set to county-of-holstein; the Valdemar IV page has 'much of the kingdom had been pledged to Holstein nobles' and Vordingborg as 'the main headquarters of the Holsteiners'.

region.text: the 12 southern-Jutland cells in the 1333 shape and not in the 1344 shape

ledger.note: 1344: southern Jutland is held by the Danish Magnates in Cliopatria. The Valdemar IV page dates only 'North Friesland was recovered in 1344' and the repayment of Jutland's mortgage is undated; the 12 cells are Cliopatria's row 'Danish Magnates'.

region.text: North Friesland, the Schleswig west coast

ledger.note: 1344: North Friesland is recovered. 'In 1344' Valdemar recovered North Friesland from its mortgagees; the cells were inside Cliopatria's Danish shape all along. Reviewer eu-14-d: counterpart set to county-of-holstein; the Valdemar IV page has 'much of the kingdom had been pledged to Holstein nobles' and Vordingborg as 'the main headquarters of the Holsteiners'.

region.text: all of Zealand

ledger.note: 1346: Valdemar retakes Zealand. 'In 1346, he took back Vordingborg Castle', and 'By the end of that year, Valdemar could claim all of Zealand as his own.' The island was inside Cliopatria's Danish shape all along. Reviewer eu-14-d: counterpart set to county-of-holstein; the Valdemar IV page has 'much of the kingdom had been pledged to Holstein nobles' and Vordingborg as 'the main headquarters of the Holsteiners'.

region.text: northern Estonia: Harria, Vironia and Jerwia, the 60 Estonian cells of Cliopatria's 1220 shape

ledger.note: 1346: Estonia is sold. Infobox 'Duke of Estonia 1340-1346', 'for 19,000 marks Valdemar gave up Danish Estonia'; the body text names the Teutonic Knights as buyer, the infobox the Livonian Order, and the page gives no year for the sale in the text (the danish-magnates dossier has 1 November 1346 and the Teutonic Order).

region.text: the 12 southern-Jutland cells in the 1352 shape and not in the 1344 shape

ledger.note: 1352: the southern-Jutland cells return to the Danish shape. Cliopatria's Danish Magnates row ends in 1351; the History of Denmark page says Valdemar IV 'gradually began to recover the territories, which was finally completed in 1360' and does not date this step.

region.text: Scania, Halland and Blekinge

ledger.note: 1360: Valdemar IV takes back Scania, Halland and Blekinge. 'forced Magnus to give up Helsingborg in 1360'; 'Halland, Blekinge, and Scania' are listed as captured, with no date for the last two (the year follows Helsingborg).

region.text: Gotland

ledger.note: 1361: Valdemar IV conquers Gotland. 'invaded Gotland in 1361'; the infobox lists 'King of the Goths' for 1361-1375. The day (27 July, Visby) is not on the page.

region.text: the Danish shape of 1395-1396

ledger.note: 17 June 1397: Denmark joins Norway and Sweden in the Kalmar Union. 'in what became known as the Kalmar Union, made official in 1397'; infobox 'Incorporated into the Kalmar Union: 17 June 1397'. The kalmar-union dossier draws the union's land from here.

wars.name: Otto II's invasion of Denmark
wars.outcome: Harald attacked Saxony in 973; Otto II counter-attacked in 974 and took Haithabu and the Dannevirke; Harald regained some of the seized territory in 983, after Otto II's defeat.
wars.note: The page calls the extent in Jutland a possibility ('possibly large parts of Jutland').

wars.name: Sweyn Forkbeard's conquest of England
wars.outcome: Sweyn was acknowledged king by December 1013 and died on 3 February 1014; the English recalled Aethelred and Cnut left.

wars.name: Cnut's conquest of England
wars.outcome: Wessex submitted late in 1015; after Assandun (18 October 1016) the land north of the Thames went to Cnut and, on Edmund's death on 30 November, the whole kingdom.

wars.name: Sweyn Estridsson's war with Harald Hardrada
wars.outcome: Harald sacked Hedeby in 1050 and Aarhus; Sweyn nearly died at the naval Battle of Nisa off Halland in 1062; 'Harald relinquished his claims to Denmark in 1064'. No border changed.
wars.note: The page dates the war only by these actions; Magnus's war with Sweyn 'lasted until 1045'.

wars.name: Danish conquest of Rugen

zones.text: Rugen: the 13 cells of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern in the 1169 shape

wars.outcome: Valdemar and Absalon gained a foothold on the southern Baltic shore; the principality became a Danish vassal until 1325.

wars.name: Canute VI's Pomeranian war
wars.outcome: Barbarossa demanded in 1184 that Canute acknowledge him as liege; Canute 'ordered two invasions of Pomerania and in 1185 forced Bogislaw to acknowledge Canute as his overlord'.
wars.note: The page does not date the invasions or the fleet action off Rugen.

wars.name: Valdemar II's campaign in Holstein and Lubeck
wars.outcome: Stellau 1201, Holstein and Lubeck conquered in 1203 (lead: 1207); Hamburg conquered in 1216.
wars.note: The page's lead and body disagree on the year of the Holstein and Lubeck conquest.

wars.name: Danish conquest of northern Estonia

zones.text: northern Estonia: Harria, Vironia and Jerwia, the 60 Estonian cells of Cliopatria's 1220 shape

wars.outcome: Danish rule established in Estonia in 1219 after the Battle of Lindanise (15 June 1219); a fortress ordered at Reval.

wars.name: Valdemar II's captivity and the Battle of Bornhoved
wars.outcome: Valdemar and his son abducted in 1223 by Count Henry I of Schwerin; Danish defeat at Molln in 1225; Bornhoved on 22 July 1227 'cemented the loss of Denmark's north German territories'.
wars.note: The release date is not on the page.

wars.name: Valdemar IV's recovery of the kingdom
wars.outcome: North Friesland recovered in 1344, Vordingborg and all Zealand in 1346, Helsingborg given up by Magnus in 1360.
wars.note: The History of Denmark page: the recovery 'was finally completed in 1360'.

wars.name: Danish conquest of Gotland
wars.outcome: Valdemar IV invaded Gotland in 1361 and took the title 'King of the Goths' (1361-1375).

wars.name: Danish-Hanseatic war
wars.outcome: 'In 1362 the Hansa states, Sweden, and Norway allied against Valdemar'; he left Denmark at Easter 1368 and 'was forced to sign the Treaty of Stralsund in 1370'. The page gives no territorial term.
wars.note: Zones empty: the Treaty of Stralsund's terms are not on the page.

certainty.note: Viking-Age and Valdemarian frontiers are approximate: the Schleswig border (Hedeby, Dannevirke), Scania and the Norwegian and English holdings; the pages give no survey or treaty line. The vassal edges (Rugen, Pomerania, Mecklenburg, Estonia) are soft.
After Bornhoved the frontier follows the Eider and the sea; the pages give no treaty line (the Treaty of Stralsund, 1370, is not described). Estonia's edge and the 1332-1360 pledges are soft.

sources.title: Danish Realm
sources.note: The assigned article: modern realm only (infobox: unification c. 965, Denmark 42,926 km2); the one medieval sentence is that the Faroes and Greenland have been under the Crown since 1397.

sources.title: Harald Bluetooth
sources.note: Reign c. 958-986, Norway c. 970-985/986, the 974 and 983 Hedeby episode; silent on Scania's year and on a capital.

sources.title: Cnut the Great

sources.title: Sweyn II of Denmark

sources.title: Canute VI of Denmark
sources.note: Reign 1182-1202, Pomerania's homage in 1185, the 1203 surrender of Adolf of Holstein's lands, Estonian crusade of 1197.

sources.title: Valdemar II of Denmark
sources.note: Holstein and Lubeck 1203, Hamburg 1216, Lindanise 15 June 1219, capture 1223, Molln 1225, Bornhoved 22 July 1227; silent on 1206, 1227 in Estonia and 1238.

sources.title: Valdemar IV of Denmark
sources.note: Acclamation 24 June 1340, North Friesland 1344, Zealand 1346, Helsingborg 1360, Gotland 1361, Stralsund 1370; silent on the sale year of Estonia and on the Scanian pledge.

notes: Page budget 9 of 9 opened, all listed; one title tried first would not load: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Denmark_(800–1523) (url_not_found). WHAT THIS DOSSIER IS: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Denmark 936-1406 read as one state to the Kalmar Union on 17 June 1397; the 1402-1406 shape is a 73 km2 stray in Finland (wrong, empty correction). THE 1018-1055 GAP: Cliopatria has no Danish shape between 1018 and 1055; the land is drawn by north-sea-empire (to 1035), denmark-england (1040-1042) and norway-denmark (1042-1047). This dossier loses Denmark to them (1018, 1040) and regains it (1035, 1047) and supplies new keyframes for 1035-1039 and 1047-1055. VASSAL POLICY: lands with their own dossiers are removed from the Danish shapes and carried as vassals so that no cell is drawn twice: Rugen (principality-of-rugen 1168-1325), Mecklenburg and Pomerania (1185-1227; Cliopatria draws them as Danish territory from 1177 and 1188), Estonia (danish-estonia 1219-1346). Norway is a vassal 1000-1015 (Sweyn's jarls). If the renderer prefers direct control, restore the Cliopatria shapes. OPEN SIBLING CONFLICTS: danish-magnates draws Estonia 1333-1343 and south Jutland 1344-1351 (here: danish-estonia holds Estonia until 1346, and the Jutland cells are split off in 1344 and regained in 1352); old-kingdom-of-norway has Viken lost to Denmark 1000-1015 and regained, while this dossier has the whole of Norway as vassal; holy-roman-empire and county-of-holstein date the Holstein occupation 1201 (here: contest 1201, conquest 1203, per Valdemar II page). DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN PAGES: Norway under Harald (infobox c. 970-985/986, the lead 'a few years in the 970s'); who added Scania (Harald, Cliopatria 960, or Sweyn); the Holstein conquest year (Valdemar II page body 1203, lead 1207); the buyer of Estonia (Teutonic Knights in the text, Livonian Order in the infobox); Valdemar IV's death (24 or 25 October 1375). NOT ON THE PAGES: the Treaty of Stensby (1238), the loss of Estonia in 1227, the Saaremaa expedition (1206-1209 shape unverified), Wendish crusade of 1147, the Hanseatic hold on Scania after 1370, Margaret's regency before 1387 and Greenland's passing in 1397; keyframes 1206, 1236 and 1250 are unverified (page budget). RULERS: only reigns the pages give; 1076-1182, 1241-1319 and 1375-1387 are missing (a gap-filler should read List of Danish monarchs). The interregnum 1332-1340 has no entry. GAZETTEER: Rugen/Arkona, Viken, North Friesland and Vordingborg are not names (used coordinates or an intersection). Hanseatic League needs a dossier (belligerent 1362-1370).
